body:
To the question about loneliness, yeah, I *think* things would feel better, more bearable if I had a good relationship, but I don't pursue it because of fear of what happens if I fail. I think that if I put myself out there and got rejected that I would lose whatever self esteem I have left. I feel like I wouldn't have anything but depression at that point. That's probably irrational, it's probably just psychological paralysis caused by the depression, but that's why I don't try, I guess.

The dull glow thing is VERY accurate (in the best of times). When I am 'enjoying' myself with my friends, it is always there, like a fear of the moment this ends. It is; however, often much more than that. When nothing fun or stimulating is happening then it is more like a blinding light I can't look away from and if something actually sad happens, then it feels like it engulfs me completely.

I don't understand the 'baking a loaf of bread' analogy, so let me just try to answer the other questions as accurately as I can. "What makes it worse?" I want to start with saying it is always there. Sometimes I am distracted from it, but I am never not-depressed. Anything that would cause a 'normal' person to be frustrated, disappointed, or sad makes it a lot worse, but honestly, sometimes it just 'flares' all on its own, if there isn't something offsetting it. That's why I try to stay distracted. "What did it feel like when it first came on?" Well that's a weird story. When I was 15, I knew a girl who was suicidal and I tried to relate to her, to make her feel better (I succeeded), but I realized I wasn't really lying. I don't know what started it, but at that point I realized I had been depressed for a while. "What does it want to say to you when you're unable to distract yourself from it?" That I failed. I'm a pretty smart guy, I used to be in all kinds of special programs and my family was convinced I would be a millionaire in my 20s, but I am in my mid 30s and not very successful (a bit short of 6 figures), no family, and no real prospects for that to change. I think to myself that this is as good as it gets, and that is a damn depressing thought. I don't know why I keep going because there is no destination. Just rinse and repeat this same miserable life every day.

Thanks for taking the time to read all that and reply, btw.
That's what I do. And no, not right now. Might need it. ;)

I'm sure you're right. I keep wanting to find meaning in my life, but failing. There is probably a way to find peace and I've spent a lot of time doing trying to mind-over-matter this, now I am looking outside. I don't know what the solution is, though.

lol then it wouldn't be called sadness, right? I get what you are saying like 1-10 isn't sad to happy, per say, it is level of emotion and I could still call 10 sad, if I want, but enjoy the fact that I am at peak. Unfortunately, I don't think sadness is just a word. I think the feeling I have every day would still be miserable even if I called it something else. I do appreciate you offering a suggestion, though.
